classification.difficultyReason: Must translate equal baseline segments into three tangent ratios and choose to combine the first two marked angles through the tangent sum formula before completing the angle proof.

spec.description: Horizontal A–B–C–D baseline; E vertically above D; AE, BE and CE meet E. Matching double ticks on AB, BC, CD and DE. Unlabelled angle arcs at A, B and C; vertex labels below the baseline and E above.
spec.mathematics: AB=BC=CD=DE; marked angles A=EAD, B=EBD and C=ECD. Coordinate ratios express the supplied equal lengths without adding numerical givens.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied geometry and givens are visible; no tangent values or angle answers.

answer.short:
$A+B=45^\circ$ and $C=45^\circ$, so $A+B+C=90^\circ$.

Use $\tan A=\frac13$, $\tan B=\frac12$ and the tangent sum expansion.
answer.worked:
The marked angles are acute. Since $AB=BC=CD=DE$,
$$\begin{align*}\tan A&=\frac{DE}{AD}=\frac13,\\\tan B&=\frac{DE}{BD}=\frac12,\\\tan C&=\frac{DE}{CD}=1.\end{align*}$$
Using the tangent sum expansion,
$$\begin{align*}\tan(A+B)&=\frac{\tan A+\tan B}{1-\tan A\tan B}\\\tan(A+B)&=\frac{\frac13+\frac12}{1-\frac13\cdot\frac12}\\\tan(A+B)&=1.\end{align*}$$
Since $0^\circ<A+B<180^\circ$, $A+B=45^\circ$. Also, $C=45^\circ$ because $C$ is acute and $\tan C=1$.
$$A+B+C=45^\circ+45^\circ=90^\circ.$$
